candidate.title: Two Tickets to the Haunted Hayride

evidence_notes.source: Full read of all 30 chapters of the finished manuscript (scratchpad hr/draft_v2.md, 68,788 parsed words), 2026-10-06. Measured from the text only; no planning files (story bible, chapter map, concept candidates, architecture fingerprint) were read. Mechanical form data from series_diff.py (prior: twin_sister.md) on this file.
evidence_notes.lane: Shelf lane sweet_small_town_holiday_second_chance (closed-door, Halloween/fall-festival season). Sub-lane: second chance with ex-fiance under forced public proximity.
evidence_notes.relationship_start: Engaged Dec 2017 (barn-loft proposal, Polaroid Ch24); she ended it Oct 6 2019, 20 days before the wedding, by putting the garnet ring by the rooster salt shaker: 'Go. Don't call. If you're going, go.' (Ch4, 5, 16). Seven years of no contact; he returned summer 2026 after his theater shop folded (Ch2).
evidence_notes.opening_engine: Ch1: at a 90-person town supper the heroine, as chair, draws guide pairs from a jar under rules she wrote and laminated (rule 7 no swaps; rule 12 chair who breaks a rule steps down). She draws herself, then him; the vice-chair publicly offers a redraw; she cites rule seven.
evidence_notes.inciting_event: Function class: forced proximity by chance, made binding by the heroine's public refusal to redraw (Ch1). It is aggravated by the fact that she has publicly cast him for six years as the villain of the ghost story the event sells (Ch1, 2, 3). Inciting KIND = choice_under_pressure.
evidence_notes.heroine_goal: Function class save_asset: the hayride needs $29,000 by Jan 1 for a new wagon or the insurer drops it (Ch3 chalkboard; Ch5 'If we don't make it, Great Lakes drops us and there is no hayride'). Secondary, emerging goal: stop telling a story she knows is untrue (Ch5 'always both').
evidence_notes.external_engine: Ten-night (Fri/Sat in October) hayride run: seven rides a night, finale at the pond, chalkboard tally each night ($2,300 Ch3 -> $13,900 Ch8 -> $16,200 Ch12 -> $21,900 Ch19 -> $29,350 Ch23 -> $36,410 FINAL Ch29). The committee votes on the finale script (rule three).
evidence_notes.agency_pattern: The heroine drives the plot by revising her own published story in escalating steps: pencils in 'Maybe still deciding' (Ch5), says it aloud and is warned 4-1 (Ch6), withdraws the story under the author clause (Ch11), replaces it with a true story given by its owner (Ch14), apologises privately (Ch22), then confesses publicly from the dock (Ch28) and enforces rule twelve on herself (Ch29).
evidence_notes.hero_error: He obeyed 'go' because it was easy and made it her fault: 'Not calling was the easiest thing I ever did... You'd told me not to, so I had permission' (Ch6); 'You said go and I went, because it was easy' (Ch24). He would not have come back if the job hadn't ended (Ch23). NOTE: the book's dominant flaw is the heroine's pre-emptive send-away ('You say go first... so it's your idea and not theirs', Ch25), which also hit her mother (Ch25) and her brother (Ch25).
evidence_notes.power_configuration: She chairs the event, wrote its bylaws and its story, and the town and vice-chair take her side; he has no institutional standing and is publicly cast as the villain (popcorn Ch4, chants Ch4, newspaper Ch22). Countervailing: a loving ally (Bev) controls the committee vote and the press.
evidence_notes.containment: Rule seven: a guide who leaves her draw leaves the season (Ch1). Ten nights on a two-seat belted front bench; rule one: guides stay belted barn to barn (Ch2). He offers her an exit twice (Ch1 'I could say I've got a conflict'; Ch3) and she refuses.
evidence_notes.midpoint_reversal: Ch14 (of 30), carried through Ch15-17: the elder tells the true 1958 search for her late husband as a boy; the heroine asks the owner first, then the committee adopts it 4-3; the couple co-build it in his barn; first performance works (Ch17). Flips: lie removed -> truth told; bench adversaries -> co-builders; money loss -> recovery. Cost: the vice-chair's open break ('Don't ask me to cry at it', Ch14), and the old story is still alive in the press (Ch16, 22).
evidence_notes.darkest_moment_cause: Class repeated_core_harm, heroine-side, on a goal collision. Her last question gets a true 'No' (he would not have come back if the job hadn't ended, Ch23); he discloses a Chicago head-of-shop offer in person (Ch21, 24); she says 'Go' again (Ch24). He refuses to let her decide for him; he walks home leaving his truck (Ch24); she sits with the rooster salt shaker and her brother names the pattern (Ch25). The newspaper cementing the false version is the external pressure (Ch22).
evidence_notes.climax: Ch28, last ride on Halloween: she tells the true story first, has the tractor driver hold the silence, unbuckles (breaking rule one), walks the dock, lifts the un-veiled lantern off its line, and retells the original story truthfully: 'She was never waiting. She sent him.' A child asks 'Is that true?'; a rider asks where the groom is; he answers from the bench, belted: 'Right here. Choosing this one.' Riders lift their lanterns toward the bench. Coda Ch29: in the shed she reads rule one and rule twelve aloud and steps down; the vice-chair says 'I was wrong' and takes the handbook.
evidence_notes.staging: venue: the finale stop of a performed attraction (dock and wagon at the pond) = stage_or_broadcast. audience: 32 paying riders, mostly strangers, plus the vice-chair, a child and the tractor driver (not the whole town). evidence: confession. authority: her own choice (she breaks the rule and later enforces its penalty on herself). spectacle: no sound; 'the thing a room does when it turns... only this time nobody looked at him', then lanterns lifted toward the bench (Ch28).
evidence_notes.repair_mechanism: Inverted grovel. Hero side, sustained truthful presence: apology asking nothing (Ch3); one true answer a night (ring sold Ch4; not calling Ch6; hated the whistle Ch11; Kate Ch13; his want Ch17; diner vigil Ch18; 'No' Ch23); cues his own villain role without defending himself (Ch3-10, 'It's her story' to the press Ch22); dunk tank (Ch7); holds the light, never fixes (Ch8); tells her he knows what tomorrow is and leaves it there (Ch20; rev: porch-light repair cut, she fixes it herself); declines the offer for his own reasons and reports the real cost (Ch26). Heroine side, staged public confession: softened line (Ch6, fails), withdrawal (Ch11), 'I'm sorry' (Ch22), dock confession (Ch28), self-enforced step-down (Ch29), 'Stay' (Ch30).
evidence_notes.resolution_visibility: Community witnessed: 32 riders (Ch28), the whole committee and volunteers in the shed (Ch29), the next-morning strike (Ch30). The 'I love you' (Ch29) and the Tuesday terms (Ch30) are private.
evidence_notes.ending_state: Full reconciliation: love declared (Ch29); he announces a proposal is coming and she answers with her own terms, 'When you ask, ask on a Tuesday... And the answer's yes' (Ch30); he writes TUES in the frost. Ring was sold (Ch4), so no ring.
evidence_notes.pov_structure: Close third person, past tense, alternating by chapter: Roz 18 chapters (1,3,5,6,8,10,11,13,14,16,18,20,22,23,25,27,28,30; 29.2k narration words), Gus 12 (2,4,7,9,12,15,17,19,21,24,26,29; 20.0k). Linear, about five weeks (Harvest Supper late Sept -> Nov 1).
evidence_notes.setting_function: The event's bylaws are the book's law (rules 1, 3, 7, 12 drive containment, the warning, the withdrawal, the climax transgression and the step-down). The wagon bench is the containment and the stage; the pond finale is the arena where the public story is told; the town (diner pie poll, Facebook, newspaper, committee votes) is audience and jury.
evidence_notes.relocation_reset: Hero relocated before page one: bought his mother's house and his father's pole barn (Ch2). The heroine never moves; she lives in her late father's house with her brother. No protective cohabitation.
evidence_notes.intimacy_function: Closed door. Two kisses, both initiated by her: corn maze at midnight, short and cold, interrupted by a raccoon (Ch18), marks her choice; on the wagon bench in the dark shed (Ch29) confirms repair. Plus hand-on-bench touches (Ch19, 27).
evidence_notes.supporting_cast_function: A town chorus with voting power. The committee votes three times (warning 4-1 Ch6; heritage plaque 4-3 Ch10; new finale 4-3 Ch14). Truth witnesses: the brother overheard the breakup from the stairs (Ch16); the best friend saw his diner vigil (Ch16); the silent volunteer says 'That story's mean' (Ch5, 10). The vice-chair is the loving antagonist who institutionalises the lie (Ch9, 10, 16, 22) and concedes (Ch29).
evidence_notes.epilogue_design: No time skip. Ch30 is the next morning: the town strikes the hayride; she names her own terms (ask on a Tuesday); two ticket halves go into a new cigar box; the Bride's lantern is hung on the empty hook in the barn.
evidence_notes.signature_scenes_more: Also: popcorn thrown and the ride stopped (Ch4); kitchen-sink sprayer hose saves the fog pump (Ch8); mud-hitch repair with a radio-host monologue (Ch13); brother reveals he heard the breakup from the stairs, father's toolbox handed over (Ch16); corn-maze kiss and raccoon (Ch18); she fixes her own porch light on the anniversary eve (Ch20, rev); Danny offers 'Stay... It's shorter than go' (Ch25), refused at Ch30 for her own terms ('ask on a Tuesday', rev); door with name and hours hung (Ch26); riders lift lanterns to the bench (Ch28); step-down by rule twelve (Ch29).
evidence_notes.first_irreversible_decision: Ch11: withdraws the Lantern Bride mid-season under the author clause of rule three. Price: about $2,800-3,000 that night (Ch12), refunds to 12 fans ($180), the vice-chair's hurt ('Is this for him?'). The Ch6 line change was a probe that she reversed under a formal warning.
evidence_notes.shape_triple: inciting kind choice_under_pressure (honouring a chance draw against a public offer to redraw, Ch1); repair shape public_confession (inverted: the heroine confesses; hero side sustained_presence); ending image object_at_rest (unlit, unveiled lantern hung on the empty hook, Ch30; the lantern is planted Ch3 and the hook/collar Ch1).
evidence_notes.technique_bank: First attraction beat Ch1 (her POV) = first-inspection line, true rather than misjudged ('He looks like somebody let him out of a coat'), capped by an object-act ('He'd brought a pin.'). First care beat Ch1 = he holds still to give her a second to withdraw the ticket and offers a cover story; this is restraint as care and not a bank device. The first bank-device care is Ch6 (hand flat on the bench, removed unseen) and Ch8 (79 minutes with the Maglite = care-object-and-service). Rev: the Ch20 porch-light service act was cut; care-object-and-service now appears at Ch8 (Maglite) and Ch26 (the door, which is his own shop, not her house), and is no longer dominant in the back half. Answer-length ladder is explicit (Ch18 'The first night you said Belt... You just said a paragraph').
evidence_notes.voice_mechanical: series_diff.py: dialogue 28.5%; Ch1 184 words to first dialogue; exit kinds dialogue 50%, image/quiet 50%, decision 6.7%, named-feeling 3.3%; voice vector per 1k narration words: em dash 0.06, neg-par 0.02, filter 4.98 (Gus POV 6.02, at threshold); top 4-grams: i'm not going to x13, in the front row x12, end of the dock x11, on the far bank x11, on the way back x10.
evidence_notes.status: measured (source: manuscript). Planned rows were not consulted; drift vs plan is not assessed here.
